negative.therapist: So in this last clip, there was a very subtle thing happening. We did move into problem solving, which in and of itself isn't necessarily a problem. Let's say, for instance, I had a critical father and it was hard for me to experience that criticalness. So, the best approach in this one would have been to stay with the issue at hand, the emotion at hand longer, and be willing to experience what the therapist is experiencing too. Additionally, this is related to core competency number nine, where we're talking about the processes that occur in the moment. positive.therapist: In the segment you just saw, there was a wonderful example of interpersonal communication between the patient and her husband. One of the techniques that's been extremely helpful in IPT has been interpersonal incidents, and what those are basically are a description of a communication, specifically not a global communication, but a specific communication between the patient and somebody else close to them, in this case, the patient and her husband. So an interpersonal incident, in contrast to a general statement—in other words, a statement like, 'My husband and I never get along, we always fight'—is a specific description of an interaction that occurred. And the idea in using an interpersonal incident is to try and find out what's going wrong in the communication. What's not working well? What is the patient saying that may not be quite as adaptive? How is the other person responding to that in a way that's shutting down communication or causing more conflict? How does the patient respond to that? It literally is a description, statement by statement, about how the interaction goes from start to finish, and getting the finishing part is particularly important.

negative.therapist: Clients who are extremely distressed are one of the most difficult tasks for therapists to handle in a therapy session. What you just saw in the video there was an attempt by myself to assist Danielle through some very distressing events that have been going on for her, specifically a breakup with her boyfriend. One of the things that I hope you did see in that short vignette that you just saw was that although the therapist at some times was engaged with the client and was being somewhat empathic, the therapist was also very, very keen to move off topic, found the distress that the client was showing very difficult to tolerate and was very keen to move away from that subject matter. And even though the client continually pulled the therapy session back to the discussion of her own flaws and the problems with the breakup with her boyfriend, the therapist really wasn't getting the message there and persisted in trying to derail what the client wanted to talk about and move the content of the session away from the breakup with the boyfriend.
